Editorial Change 1 (January 2023) restores a missing table. The report states that it is not a Recommended Standard and that CCSDS 231.0-B-4 prevails in case of conflict (PDF p. 13).
summary:
The CCSDS Green Book that explains and justifies the [TC Synchronization and Channel Coding](../ccsds/tc-coding-cltu.md) Recommended Standard (231.0-B-4). That standard is the sublayer that turns variable-length [TC](../ccsds/tc-sdlp.md) or [USLP](../ccsds/uslp.md) Transfer Frames into **CLTUs** (Communications Link Transmission Units) for the uplink, and back again on board. It is the most practical companion to the Blue Book, for spacecraft telecommand-decoder designers and for ground engineers who build CLTUs (for example behind an [SLE FCLTU](../ccsds/sle/fcltu.md) service).

Section 2 lists what the sublayer does at each end. Section 3 explains the (63,56) BCH code: 56 information bits, 7 inverted parity bits and a filler bit per 64-bit codeword, frames split seven octets at a time, 0x55 fill, and why the older 40, 48 and 56-bit codewords were dropped. Section 4 explains how the short-blocklength (128,64) and (512,256) LDPC codes were chosen. Sections 5 and 6 give the CLTU format for BCH (start sequence 0xEB90, tail C5 C5 C5 C5 C5 C5 C5 79) and for LDPC (64-bit start sequence, optional tail). Section 7 covers the Physical Layer Operations Procedures PLOP-1 and PLOP-2. Section 8 walks through the on-board CLTU reception state machine (Inactive, Search, Decode). Section 9 covers the TC pseudo-randomizer, section 10 systematic retransmission for deep-space links, and section 11 gives extensive performance data: frame rejection and undetected-error rates, and LDPC decoders such as layered BP and most-reliable-basis.

The annexes give the theory behind the randomizer and tail sequences, performance of obsolete features, a go-back-n analysis with multiple copies, BCH undetected-error calculations and, most usefully, worked hexadecimal examples of real TC Transfer Frames and CLTUs with and without randomization.

key_points.text: The report is informational; CCSDS 231.0-B-4 (July 2021) is the controlling Recommended Standard.
TC Synchronization and Channel Coding is used below the TC Space Data Link Protocol or USLP for variable-length frames; TM Synchronization and Channel Coding handles fixed-length frames.
The sending-end sublayer adds error protection, delimits data units, lets the receiver resolve bit ambiguity, and (through the PLOPs) controls acquisition and idle bit patterns.
A CLTU carrying one maximum-length (1024-octet) TC Transfer Frame has 147 BCH codewords and is 1186 octets long.
A BCH codeword is 56 information bits, 7 complemented parity bits and one filler bit (always 0); I0 is transmitted first.
Codeword lengths of 40, 48 and 56 bits were dropped in June 2000 in favour of the 64-bit codeword, which has 14% bandwidth overhead (25% for the old 40-bit option).
Frame data go into BCH codewords seven octets at a time regardless of frame boundaries; the last codeword is padded with alternating 0/1 fill (0x55), up to six octets.

Uplink uses are grouped into four modes (emergency, command/ARQ, file upload, human support); the (128,64) and (512,256) LDPC codes target the first two and can replace BCH with little impact elsewhere.
With BCH coding, the CLTU Start Sequence is 0xEB90 and the 64-bit Tail Sequence is C5 C5 C5 C5 C5 C5 C5 79.
With LDPC coding, the Start Sequence is the 64-bit pattern 0347 76C7 2728 95B0; the tail sequence is optional with the (128,64) code.
PLOP-2 is required for missions whose planning began after September 2010; PLOP-1 sends an acquisition sequence before every CLTU, costing throughput but avoiding missed CLTU boundaries.

The TC randomizer (Bit Transition Generator) is an 8-bit LFSR, h(x) = x^8 + x^6 + x^4 + x^3 + x^2 + x + 1, initialised to all ones; with BCH it randomizes the 56-bit information fields (not the parity, start or tail sequences), and with LDPC it is reset for each codeword after encoding.
Annex F gives worked hexadecimal examples of TC Transfer Frames (with FECF) and the resulting BCH- and LDPC-coded CLTUs, with and without randomization.

notes: The slug's 'e1' is Editorial Change 1 (January 2023), which 'restores missing table'; the Document Control page footer shows the overlapping dates 'October 2021' and 'January 2023'. PDF pages 1 and 2 are duplicate cover pages. The extraction has 174 PDF pages (registry: 173). Reference [5] is still TM Synchronization and Channel Coding issue 3 (2017) and [2] is the 2014 issue of 130.0-G. Reference [9] is marked 'Not publicly available'. Reference [14] is an ESA paper on the Rosetta use of packet telemetry and telecommand standards. Many performance figures extract as axis labels only. For references with personal authors, the authors are put in parentheses after the title; journal or proceedings details are in doc_id. Section 1.4 is a plain 'References' list (kind 'reference'). No individual authors of the report are named.
